newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UK trade gap seen narrowing in April.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UK trade gap seen narrowing in April.

text.p: Britain's trade deficit with the rest of the world is expected to narrow in April, but the damaging impact of the pound's recent strength means the improvement may be the last for some time, analysts said.
The Reuters consensus forecast suggests the trade gap narrowed to 625 million pounds ($1 billion) in April from 671 million in March.
"We will see a deterioration later in the year but we are starting from a favourable base," said Andrew Snowball, treasury economist at the Co-operative Bank.
The figures, along with more up-to-date data for trade with non-European Union countries covering May, will be released by the Office of National Statistics (ONS) at 0830 GMT on Wednesday.
But Snowball said the longer it takes for the strong pound to affect the trade balance, the better the chances that its impact will be offset by strong economic growth overseas.
The pound has appreciated by around 19 percent on a trade-weighted basis since last August.
"I am not going to start saying this is the start of some horrendous deterioration as a result of sterling appreciation," he said.
Dharshini David, UK economist at HSBC Markets, forecasts a deficit of just 600 million pounds in April, below the market consensus.
She said April's figures would still reflect increased revenues from the stronger pound, but soon the currency's appreciation would make British exports uncompetitive and begin to bite into volumes.
"We would expect to see a considerable widening of the trade in goods deficit in the second half of the year," David said.
Economists at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell forecast an even greater fall in the deficit in April -- to 550 million pounds.
"This is mainly due to the lower non-EU deficit already reported," said economists there.

April figures for trade with countries outside the European Union showed the deficit fell to 335 million pounds from 651 million in March, with much of the improvement coming in the underlying balance, which excludes oil and erratic items.
But economists expect this improvement to be partly reversed in May. The Reuters consensus forecast suggests that deficit widened to 530 million pounds in the month.

"We expect the sharp fall in the underlying deficit to be reversed in May which, along with a small fall in the oil deficit, will give an overall non-EU deficit of 675 million pounds -- the highest since September," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell economists.
